Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html`.

{"path":"chip8_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"
Create a complete, self-contained CHIP-8 emulator in a single HTML file (no external libs/CDNs). Requirements:

1. Inline CSS + JS only, dark-themed UI, no external resources.

2. Chip8 class with: 4096 bytes memory (Uint8Array), fontset (standard 16 chars 5 bytes each, 0x50-0x9F) loaded at 0x050, programs loaded at 0x200, 16 registers V[0..15] (Uint8Array), 16-bit index register I, 16-bit program counter PC starting at 0x200, 16-level call stack (array) with stack pointer, delay timer DT and sound timer ST (decremented at 60Hz via a separate timer independent from the CPU instruction loop), 64x32 display buffer (Uint8Array of 2048, 0/1), keypad state array of 16 booleans, drawFlag.

3. Implement full 35-instruction CHIP-8 opcode set, decoded from two bytes big-endian:
00E0 CLS, 00EE RET, 1NNN JP addr, 2NNN CALL addr, 3XKK SE Vx,byte, 4XKK SNE Vx,byte, 5XY0 SE Vx,Vy, 6XKK LD Vx,byte, 7XKK ADD Vx,byte (no carry, wraps 8-bit), 8XY0 LD Vx,Vy, 8XY1 OR, 8XY2 AND, 8XY3 XOR, 8XY4 ADD Vx,Vy with VF=carry, 8XY5 SUB Vx,Vy with VF=NOT borrow, 8XY6 SHR Vx (VF=LSB before shift), 8XY7 SUBN Vx,Vy with VF=NOT borrow, 8XYE SHL Vx (VF=MSB before shift), 9XY0 SNE Vx,Vy, ANNN LD I,addr, BNNN JP V0,addr, CXKK RND Vx,byte AND kk, DXYN DRW Vx,Vy,nibble (XOR sprite rows from memory[I..I+n-1] onto display with wraparound, VF=1 if any pixel collision/erased), EX9E SKP Vx (skip if key Vx pressed), EXA1 SKNP Vx (skip if key Vx not pressed), FX07 LD Vx,DT, FX0A LD Vx,K (blocking wait for keypress - halt PC advance until a key is released after being pressed, store key), FX15 LD DT,Vx, FX18 LD ST,Vx, FX1E ADD I,Vx, FX29 LD F,Vx (I = sprite addr for digit Vx, at 0x050 + Vx*5), FX33 LD B,Vx (BCD of Vx into memory[I],[I+1],[I+2]), FX55 LD [I],Vx (store V0..Vx into memory starting at I, I unmodified in this implementation, classic behavior comment optional), FX65 LD Vx,[I] (load V0..Vx from memory starting at I). That is the full 35-instruction set.

4. Each executed instruction must produce a short decoded mnemonic string (e.g. "DRW V0, V1, 5") stored for the debugger panel.

5. Display: a <canvas> 64x32 logical pixels scaled up (e.g. 10x or CSS scaling) to something like 640x320 displayed, rendered with 2D context, pixel-on = light color, pixel-off = dark background, redraw only when drawFlag is set.

6. Keypad: show a 4x4 grid of labeled buttons in the UI representing CHIP-8 keys 0-F arranged in standard layout (1 2 3 C / 4 5 6 D / 7 8 9 E / A 0 B F), each button visually highlights when pressed. Map keyboard keys 1234/qwer/asdf/zxcv to CHIP-8 keys 1,2,3,C / 4,5,6,D / 7,8,9,E / A,0,B,F respectively. Handle both keydown (set key pressed=true, preventDefault) and keyup (set pressed=false) on window, plus mousedown/mouseup (and touchstart/touchend) on the on-screen buttons so clicking/tapping also sends press AND release to the emulator (use pointerdown/pointerup or mousedown/mouseup+mouseleave to ensure release fires).

7. Demo ROM: embed this exact byte array (hand-assembled CHIP-8 program, 32 bytes) as a built-in default ROM that loads automatically on page load, draws the digit-0 font sprite at (28,12), then blocks waiting for a keypress; if key 7 is pressed moves the sprite left by 1 pixel, if key 9 is pressed moves it right by 1 pixel (any other key just redraws), then loops forever waiting for the next key — this demonstrates sprite drawing, XOR erase/redraw, and key-reactive movement:
[0x60,0x1C, 0x61,0x0C, 0x62,0x00, 0xF2,0x29, 0xD0,0x15, 0xF3,0x0A, 0xD0,0x15, 0x33,0x07, 0x12,0x16, 0x70,0xFF, 0x12,0x1C, 0x33,0x09, 0x12,0x1C, 0x70,0x01, 0xD0,0x15, 0x12,0x06]
Label this array clearly with a comment explaining the assembly (instruction by instruction) above it.

8. File loading: an <input type="file"> to load a .ch8/.bin ROM from disk via FileReader as ArrayBuffer, which resets the emulator and loads the chosen ROM at 0x200 instead of the demo.

9. Controls (all must be functional): Run (starts the execution loop via requestAnimationFrame or setInterval, running N instructions per frame as configured), Pause (stops the loop without resetting state), Step (executes exactly one instruction while paused, updates debugger and display), Reset (reinitializes memory/registers/stack/display/timers and reloads the currently selected ROM — demo or last loaded file), a numeric/range input for "instructions per frame" (e.g. range 1-200, default ~10), a visible readout of current speed value. The 60Hz delay/sound timer countdown must run on its own fixed-rate interval (e.g. setInterval 1000/60) independent of the instructions-per-frame execution speed, and should tick even while a single Step is used repeatedly is not required but while Running it must be correct 60Hz.

10. Debugger panel, continuously updated: a grid/table of all 16 registers V0-VF in hex, the I register in hex, the PC in hex, DT and ST values, the call stack contents (addresses, with stack pointer indicator), and the current decoded instruction mnemonic plus its raw hex opcode. Update this panel after every step/frame.

11. Sound: when ST > 0 optionally show a visual beep indicator (e.g. a label "BEEP" or flashing element) — do not require actual audio output, but you may optionally use a simple WebAudio beep while ST>0; this is optional polish, visual indicator is sufficient and simpler/safer.

12. Clean modern dark UI with clear sections: canvas/display, keypad, controls, speed slider, ROM loader, debugger panel. All labeled. No external fonts/libraries/images. Everything inline in this one HTML file.

Write the complete file now.
"}
